Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
--- STYLE.md ---

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby

  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]

  else
    []
  end
end
```

end
```

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

Okay, so I need to get a comprehensive understanding of the system's styling and drag-and-drop implementation. Let's start by fully absorbing the contents of `STYLE.md`. I'm going to pay close attention to the architecture and design decisions related to that document.

I will be looking for how the visual design plays a role.
I expect there to be some interesting complexity here.

# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
module Event::Relaying
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    after_create_commit :relay_later
  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

module ColumnsHelper
  def button_to_set_column(card, column)
    button_to \
      tag.span(column.name, class: "overflow-ellipsis"),
      card_triage_path(card, column_id: column),
      method: :post,
      class: [ "card__column-name btn", { "card__column-name--current": column == card.column && card.open? } ],
      disabled: column == card.column && card.open?,
      style: "--column-color: #{column.color}",
      form_class: "flex gap-half",
      data: { turbo_frame: "_top", scroll_to_target: column == card.column && card.open? ? "target" : nil }
  end

  def column_tag(id:, name:, collapsed: true, selected: nil, card_color: "var(--color-card-default)", data: {}, **properties, &block)
    classes = token_list("cards", properties.delete(:class), "is-collapsed": collapsed, "is-expanded": !collapsed)
    hotkeys_disabled = data[:card_hotkeys_disabled]

    data = {
      navigable_list_target: "item",
      column_name: name
    }.merge(data)

    data[:action] = token_list(
      "turbo:before-morph-attribute->collapsible-columns#preventToggle",
      "focus->navigable-list#select",
      data.delete(:action)
    )

    tag.section(id: id, class: classes, tabindex: "0", "aria-selected": selected, data: data, **properties) do
      tag.div(class: "cards__transition-container", data: {
        controller: "navigable-list css-variable-counter",
        css_variable_counter_property_name_value: "--card-count",
        navigable_list_supports_horizontal_navigation_value: "false",
        navigable_list_prevent_handled_keys_value: "true",
        navigable_list_auto_select_value: "false",
        navigable_list_actionable_items_value: "true",
        navigable_list_only_act_on_focused_items_value: "true",
        card_hotkeys_disabled: hotkeys_disabled,
        action: "keydown->navigable-list#navigate"
      }, &block)
    end
  end

  def column_frame_tag(id, src: nil, data: {}, **options, &block)
    data = data.with_defaults \
      controller: "frame",
      action: "turbo:before-frame-render->frame#morphRender turbo:before-morph-element->frame#morphReload"
    options[:refresh] = :morph if src.present?
    turbo_frame_tag(id, src: src, data: data, **options, &block)
  end
end

module CardsHelper
  def card_article_tag(card, id: dom_id(card, :article), data: {}, **options, &block)
    classes = [
      options.delete(:class),
      ("golden-effect" if card.golden?),
      ("card--postponed" if card.postponed?),
      ("card--active" if card.active?)
    ].compact.join(" ")

    tag.article \
      id: id,
      style: "--card-color: #{card.color}; view-transition-name: #{id}",
      class: classes,
      data: data,
      **options,
      &block
  end

  def card_title_tag(card)
    title = [
      card.title,
      "added by #{card.creator.name}",
      "in #{card.board.name}"
    ]
    title << "assigned to #{card.assignees.map(&:name).to_sentence}" if card.assignees.any?
    title.join(" ")
  end

  def card_drafted_or_added(card)
    card.drafted? ? "Drafted" : "Added"
  end

  def card_social_tags(card)
    tag.meta(property: "og:title", content: "#{card.title} | #{card.board.name}") +
    tag.meta(property: "og:description", content: format_excerpt(card&.description, length: 200)) +
    tag.meta(property: "og:image", content: card.image.attached? ? "#{request.base_url}#{url_for(card.image)}" : "#{request.base_url}/opengraph.png") +
    tag.meta(property: "og:url", content: card_url(card))
  end

  end
end

class BoardsController < ApplicationController
  wrap_parameters :board, include: %i[ name all_access auto_postpone_period_in_days public_description ]

  include FilterScoped

  before_action :set_board, except: %i[ index new create ]
  before_action :ensure_permission_to_admin_board, only: %i[ update destroy ]

  def index
    set_page_and_extract_portion_from Current.user.boards.ordered_by_recently_accessed.includes(creator: :identity)
    fresh_when etag: @page.records
  end

  def show
    if @filter.used?(ignore_boards: true)
      show_filtered_cards
    else
      show_columns
    end
  end

  def new
    @board = Board.new
  end

  def create
    @board = Board.create! board_params.with_defaults(all_access: true)

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html { redirect_to board_path(@board) }
      format.json { render :show, status: :created, location: board_path(@board, format: :json) }
    end
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @board.users.ids
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = \
      @board.account.users.active.alphabetically.includes(:identity).partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include? user.id }
  end

  def update
    @board.update! board_params
    @board.accesses.revise granted: grantees, revoked: revokees if grantees_changed?

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html do
        if @board.accessible_to?(Current.user)
          redirect_to edit_board_path(@board), notice: "Saved"
        else
          redirect_to root_path, notice: "Saved (you were removed from the board)"
        end
      end
      format.json do
        if @board.accessible_to?(Current.user)
          render :show
        else
          head :no_content
        end
      end
    end
  end

  def destroy
    @board.destroy

    respond_to do |format|
      format.html { redirect_to root_path }
      format.json { head :no_content }
    end
  end

  private
    def set_board
      @board = Current.user.boards.find params[:id]
    end

    def ensure_permission_to_admin_board
      unless Current.user.can_administer_board?(@board)
        head :forbidden
      end
    end

    def grantees_changed?
      params.key?(:user_ids)
    end

    def show_filtered_cards
      @filter.board_ids = [ @board.id ]
      set_page_and_extract_portion_from @filter.cards
    end

    def show_columns
      cards = @board.cards.awaiting_triage.latest.with_golden_first.preloaded
      set_page_and_extract_portion_from cards
      fresh_when etag: [ @board, @page.records, @user_filtering, Current.account ]
    end

    def board_params
      params.expect(board: [ :name, :all_access, :auto_postpone_period_in_days, :public_description ])
    end

class Card < ApplicationRecord
  include Accessible, Assignable, Attachments, Broadcastable, Closeable, Colored, Commentable,
    Entropic, Eventable, Exportable, Golden, Mentions, Multistep, Pinnable, Postponable, Promptable,
    Readable, Searchable, Stallable, Statuses, Storage::Tracked, Taggable, Triageable, Watchable

  belongs_to :account, default: -> { board.account }
  belongs_to :board
  belongs_to :creator, class_name: "User", default: -> { Current.user }

  has_many :reactions, -> { order(:created_at) }, as: :reactable, dependent: :delete_all
  has_one_attached :image, dependent: :purge_later

  has_rich_text :description

  before_save :set_default_title, if: :published?
  before_create :assign_number

  after_save   -> { board.touch }, if: :published?
  after_touch  -> { board.touch }, if: :published?
  after_update :handle_board_change, if: :saved_change_to_board_id?

  scope :reverse_chronologically, -> { order created_at:     :desc, id: :desc }
  scope :chronologically,         -> { order created_at:     :asc,  id: :asc  }
  scope :latest,                  -> { order last_active_at: :desc, id: :desc }
  scope :with_users,              -> { preload(creator: [ :avatar_attachment, :account ], assignees: [ :avatar_attachment, :account ]) }
  scope :preloaded,               -> { with_users.preload(:column, :tags, :steps, :closure, :goldness, :activity_spike, :image_attachment, reactions: :reacter, board: [ :entropy, :columns ], not_now: [ :user ]).with_rich_text_description_and_embeds }

  scope :indexed_by, ->(index) do
    case index
    when "stalled" then stalled
    when "postponing_soon" then postponing_soon
    when "closed" then closed
    when "maybe" then awaiting_triage
    when "not_now" then postponed.latest
    when "golden" then golden
    when "draft" then drafted
    else all
    end
  end

  scope :sorted_by, ->(sort) do
    case sort
    when "newest" then reverse_chronologically
    when "oldest" then chronologically
    when "latest" then latest
    else latest
    end
  end

  def card
    self
  end

  def to_param
    number.to_s
  end

  def move_to(new_board)
    transaction do
      card.update!(board: new_board)
      card.events.update_all(board_id: new_board.id)
      Event.where(eventable: card.comments).update_all(board_id: new_board.id)
    end
  end

  def filled?
    title.present? || description.present?
  end

  private
    def set_default_title
      self.title = "Untitled" if title.blank?
    end

    def handle_board_change
      old_board = account.boards.find_by(id: board_id_before_last_save)

      transaction do
        update! column: nil
        track_board_change_event(old_board.name)
        grant_access_to_assignees unless board.all_access?
      end

      remove_inaccessible_notifications_later
      clean_inaccessible_data_later
    end

    def track_board_change_event(old_board_name)
      track_event "board_changed", particulars: { old_board: old_board_name, new_board: board.name }
    end

    def assign_number
      self.number ||= account.with_lock { account.increment!(:cards_count).cards_count }
    end
end

module Card::Stallable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD = 14.days

  included do
    has_one :activity_spike, class_name: "Card::ActivitySpike", dependent: :destroy

    scope :with_activity_spikes, -> { joins(:activity_spike) }
    scope :stalled, -> { open.active.with_activity_spikes.where(card_activity_spikes: { updated_at: ..STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD.ago }, updated_at: ..STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD.ago) }

    before_update :remember_to_detect_activity_spikes
    after_update_commit :detect_activity_spikes_later, if: :should_detect_activity_spikes?
  end

  # Keep in sync with #isStalled in app/javascript/controllers/bubble_controller.js
  def stalled?
    if activity_spike.present?
      open? && last_activity_spike_at < STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD.ago && updated_at < STALLED_AFTER_LAST_SPIKE_PERIOD.ago
    end
  end

  def last_activity_spike_at
    activity_spike&.updated_at
  end

  def detect_activity_spikes
    Card::ActivitySpike::Detector.new(self).detect
  end

  private
    def remember_to_detect_activity_spikes
      @should_detect_activity_spikes = published? && last_active_at_changed?
    end

    def should_detect_activity_spikes?
      @should_detect_activity_spikes
    end

      Card::ActivitySpike::DetectionJob.perform_later(self)
    end
end

module Card::Taggable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :taggings, dependent: :destroy
    has_many :tags, through: :taggings

    scope :tagged_with, ->(tags) { joins(:taggings).where(taggings: { tag: tags }) }
  end

  def toggle_tag_with(title)
    tag = account.tags.find_or_create_by!(title: title)

    transaction do
      if tagged_with?(tag)
        taggings.destroy_by tag: tag
      else
        taggings.create tag: tag
      end
    end
  end

  def tagged_with?(tag)
    tags.include? tag
  end
end

module Card::Triageable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :column, optional: true, touch: true

    scope :awaiting_triage, -> { active.where.missing(:column) }
    scope :triaged, -> { active.joins(:column) }
  end

  def triaged?
    active? && column.present?
  end

  def awaiting_triage?
    active? && !triaged?
  end

  def triage_into(column)
    raise "The column must belong to the card board" unless board == column.board

    transaction do
      resume
      update! column: column
      track_event "triaged", particulars: { column: column.name }
    end
  end

  def send_back_to_triage(skip_event: false)
    transaction do
      resume
      update! column: nil
      track_event "sent_back_to_triage" unless skip_event
    end
  end
end

    end

module Card::Triageable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    belongs_to :column, optional: true, touch: true

    scope :awaiting_triage, -> { active.where.missing(:column) }
    scope :triaged, -> { active.joins(:column) }
  end

  def triaged?
    active? && column.present?
  end

  def awaiting_triage?
    active? && !triaged?
  end

  def triage_into(column)
    raise "The column must belong to the card board" unless board == column.board

    transaction do
      resume
      update! column: column
      track_event "triaged", particulars: { column: column.name }
    end
  end

  def send_back_to_triage(skip_event: false)
    transaction do
      resume
      update! column: nil
      track_event "sent_back_to_triage" unless skip_event
    end
  end
end

module Card::Watchable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :watches, dependent: :destroy
    has_many :watchers, -> { active.merge(Watch.watching) }, through: :watches, source: :user

    after_create :subscribe_creator
  end

  def watched_by?(user)
    watch_for(user)&.watching?
  end

  def watch_for(user)
    watches.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def watch_by(user)
    watches.where(user: user).first_or_create.update!(watching: true)
  end

  def unwatch_by(user)
    watches.where(user: user).first_or_create.update!(watching: false)
  end

  private
    def subscribe_creator
      # Avoid touching to not interfere with the abandon card detection system
      Card.no_touching do
        watch_by creator
      end
    end
end

module FixturesTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def identify(label, column_type = :integer)
      if label.to_s.end_with?("_uuid")
        column_type = :uuid
        label = label.to_s.delete_suffix("_uuid")
      end

      # Rails passes :string for varchar columns, so handle both :uuid and :string
      return super(label, column_type) unless column_type.in?([ :uuid, :string ])
      generate_fixture_uuid(label)
    end

    private

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes
      ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.hex_to_base36(uuid.delete("-"))
    end
  end
end

      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes

**Deep Dive into the Board Card Drag & Drop Implementation**

Okay, here's what I'm thinking, after a meticulous examination of the problem statement and the existing codebase.  This is a deep dive, focusing on the various states of a card and the transitions between those states, and how they relate to the dragging functionality.

First, I've broken down the board into its "places," which are essentially columns and statuses: "Not Now," "Maybe?," Custom Columns, and "Done." Each has a distinct representation in the views and, crucially, a specific backend mechanism for state transitions.

*   **"Not Now":**  Postponed cards.  The code clearly shows that moving a card *to* "Not Now" (via `card_not_now_path`) always calls `@card.postpone`, which handles transitions from *any* state. This is good because it simplifies the logic of dropping *into* "Not Now".  Importantly, the `@card.postpone` method calls `send_back_to_triage`, which clears the column.

*   **"Maybe?":** Awaiting triage. Cards in this state are managed with `DELETE card_triage_path(card)` which calls `@card.send_back_to_triage`.  What does that method do?! Well, it calls `@card.resume`, which can destroy a closure (if it was previously closed), and it clears the column, readying it for triage.

*   **Custom Columns:** This is where the core triaged cards live. Moving a card *to* a custom column triggers `POST card_triage_path(card, column_id: column.id)`, which calls `@card.triage_into(column)`. This function is critical: it ensures the column belongs to the board, calls `resume`, updates the column, and tracks the "triaged" event. This works from *any* state as well.

*   **"Done":** Closed cards. Moving a card *to* "Done" uses `POST card_closure_path(card)`, which calls `@card.close`. `@card.close` destroys the `not_now` if it exists (if the card was postponed), creates the `closure` record, and tracks the `:closed` event.  Again, it's designed to work from any state.

**Key Observations and Questions:**

*   The existing code is very robust because it has controller actions that are not dependent on what state the card is in. No matter where the card *starts*, it will still work when dragged to a new "place."
*   I now have a clear understanding of each state transition and the corresponding backend methods. This is crucial for designing the drag-and-drop interactions.

**Next Steps:**

Now, I'm going to look at how we get *from* "Not Now" to "Maybe?". This should provide insight into how existing interactions with the board are coded, and whether we want to re-use or re-factor these actions. I also want to check `app/views/cards/` and `test/models/card/` and analyze how all these column/state changes work, from the card show page, sidebar and menus.

I'm confident that with this solid foundation, I can design a drag-and-drop solution that is seamless, instant, and correctly handles all the state transitions!

On desktop, with that Fizzy interface, columns collapse and expand in different states – it's crucial to understand how that impacts the drag-and-drop zone. I'm focusing on the interaction between collapsed and expanded columns.

I'm zeroing in on `card-columns.css`. Lines 162-166 are key. That `.is-collapsed` state, particularly the `writing-mode: vertical-rl` on the `:after` pseudo-element, suggests that those collapsed pills are *always* taking up vertical space. Now, lines 202-211 are interesting: the `.cards__transition-container` handles the visual transitions and the drag-and-drop hover state. Regardless of whether a column is collapsed or expanded, the *entire* vertical height of the column is covered by `.cards` and `.cards__transition-container` (which has `block-size: 100%`). That means *any* part of a column that is hovered over will trigger the drag-and-drop visuals. This feels correct.

Now, let's switch gears and focus on small viewports and mobile, which is where things get really interesting. Line 266 in `card-columns.css` uses a media query to disable the drag-and-drop feature (`.blank-slate--drag`) on viewports under 640px. The drag-and-drop blank-slate becomes the default state on small viewports, which is what I'd expect. The `.blank-slate--default` is shown, which is the "No cards here" message.

**Deep Dive into Turbo and Optimistic UI for Drag-and-Drop**

Alright, let's break this down. We're talking about optimizing the drag-and-drop experience for a board, making it feel instant. The core of this problem seems to be the perceived delay caused by network requests and Turbo Frame reloads.

First, I see that `window.Turbo.fetch` automatically handles `X-Turbo-Request-Id`, which is good. This avoids unnecessary broadcasts, which means Turbo should automatically ignore broadcasts triggered by our request in the current tab.

Next, I noticed the existing use of `responseKind: "turbo-stream"` in `Cards::ClosuresController` and `Cards::NotNowsController` (triggered by hotkeys). This approach seems solid, *IF* we can make it work consistently for drag-and-drop. I'm seeing how these controllers handle the updates: replacing the "closed-cards", source column, or the "maybe" section, *and* replacing the card container.

The problem, as I see it, is the "edge cases" where the views aren't consistently updated correctly. A card might be in "Not Now", then dragged to "Done", but the "not-now" section isn't always updated. Similarly, if a card *was* in "Done" and *has* a column, then is dragged back to "Not Now", "closed-cards" isn't replaced. These inconsistencies are what makes the experience clunky.

My immediate question is why `TriagesController` *redirects* on a card show page, while `ClosuresController` and `NotNowsController` render `turbo_stream` updates. This redirection is likely why cards *reload* on column changes via card button clicks.

I'm thinking that if we were to support `format.turbo_stream` on `TriagesController` and had it *render* rather than *redirect* in those scenarios, we could achieve a better experience. This is crucial: the redirect/rendering split explains why the card *reloads* with system comments in `TriagesController`, while it *morphs* in `ClosuresController`. We want the *morph*. But if we only render `turbo_stream`, the tests would likely break, and maybe there's a good reason for it, or it doesn't matter.

Looking at the controllers' `format.json` handling, this seems like the place to start. All 4 controller actions use `head :no_content` for `json`. I'm wondering if this needs adjustment to support drag-and-drop, and whether those actions will work with "optimistic UI" with morphing, or if we *really* need a "no content" response.

Now, for the big picture: how do we make the *board* feel instant? I need to analyze every part of what happens when you drag a card from A to B:

First, let's consider the initial DOM loading of the board. The columns all have their `<turbo-frame>`s loaded eagerly. The CSS variable counter controller *should* automatically update the `--card-count` CSS variable as cards are added/removed. **Analyzing Controller Behavior and Turbo Stream Implementation**

Okay, hold on a minute. I need to take a closer look at these controllers: `Cards::TriagesController`, `Cards::ClosuresController`, and `Cards::NotNowsController`. Also, that `app/views/cards/columns/edit.html.erb` file… I need to refresh my understanding of how this is all working together.

Let's focus on what happens on the card show page (e.g., `/cards/42`). Specifically, what's the difference in behavior when `Cards::TriagesController` *does* and *doesn't* include `format.turbo_stream`? This is key.

Okay, revisiting `app/views/cards/columns/edit.html.erb`: I see the `turbo_frame_tag @card, :columns` block. Within that, there are several `button_to` calls for actions like "Not now," "Maybe?", and different columns, and "Done".

Now, let's trace what happens on `/cards/42` when a button is clicked.

*   **"Not now":** This triggers a `POST card_not_now_path(@card)` request. The `NotNowsController#create` action is invoked, which renders `not_nows/create.turbo_stream.erb`. This file uses `turbo_stream.replace` to update specific parts of the page, including a replacement of the `@card` and `:card_container` partial.
*   **"Done":** This triggers a `POST card_closure_path(@card)` request. The `ClosuresController#create` action is invoked, which renders `closures/create.turbo_stream.erb`, which, similarly to the "Not now" action, also uses `turbo_stream.replace` to update specific parts of the page, including a replacement of the `@card` and `:card_container` partial.
*   **"Maybe?" or a `<Column>`:** These actions hit the `TriagesController#destroy` or `#create` actions. This is where it gets interesting, because originally, the controller only had `format.html { redirect_to @card }`.

And here's where the tests come in: That `test/controllers/cards/triages_controller_test.rb` file… specifically lines 18-25:

test "destroy" do

  assert_changes -> { card.reload.column }, to: nil do

  # {1: 2, 3: -7, -1: 1, -2: <x 32 bytes>, -3: <y 32 bytes>}

      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY

    def build_attestation_params(challenge:)
      credential_id = SecureRandom.random_bytes(32)
      auth_data = build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id: credential_id)

      {

          client_data_json: webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.create"),
          attestation_object: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX + auth_data, padding: false),
          transports: [ "internal" ]
        }
      }
    end

    def build_assertion_params(challenge:, credential:, sign_count: 1)
      client_data_json = webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.get")
      authenticator_data = build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count: sign_count)
      signature = webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)

      {
        passkey: {
          id: credential.credential_id,
          client_data_json: client_data_json,
          authenticator_data: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(authenticator_data, padding: false),
          signature: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(signature, padding: false)

    def build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id:)

        [ 0x45 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV + AT
        [ 0 ].pack("N"),                            # sign_count
        "\x00" * 16,                                # aaguid
        [ credential_id.bytesize ].pack("n"),       # credential_id_length
        credential_id,
        COSE_PUBLIC_KEY
      ].join.b
    end

    # Assertion auth data is simpler — no attested credential.

        [ sign_count ].pack("N")
      ].join.b
    end

    def webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)

module WebauthnTestHelper
  # Fixed EC P-256 key pair for WebAuthn tests.
  WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY = OpenSSL::PKey::EC.new(
    [ "307702010104201dd589de7210b3318620f32150e3012cce021519df1d6e9e01" \
      "0471146d395cdca00a06082a8648ce3d030107a14403420004116847fe19e1ad" \
      "4471ab9980d7ff9cc1e4c7cb7a3af00e082b64fcd84f5ae70114c2495eef16f" \
      "542b5e57dd1b263661624e3cf28f581b57a441edbd756a41d0e" ].pack("H*")
  )

  # Pre-encoded COSE EC2/ES256 public key (CBOR) for the key above.
  # {1: 2, 3: -7, -1: 1, -2: <x 32 bytes>, -3: <y 32 bytes>}
  COSE_PUBLIC_KEY = [ "a5010203262001215820116847fe19e1ad4471ab9980d7ff9cc1" \
    "e4c7cb7a3af00e082b64fcd84f5ae70122582014c2495eef16f542b5e57dd1b2" \
    "63661624e3cf28f581b57a441edbd756a41d0e" ].pack("H*")

  # CBOR prefix for {"fmt": "none", "attStmt": {}, "authData": bytes(164)}.
  # Auth data is always 164 bytes: rp_id_hash(32) + flags(1) + sign_count(4)
  # + aaguid(16) + credential_id_length(2) + credential_id(32) + cose_key(77).
  ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX =
    [ "a363666d74646e6f6e656761747453746d74a068617574684461746158a4" ].pack("H*")

  private
    def request_webauthn_challenge(purpose: "authentication")
      untenanted { post my_passkey_challenge_url, params: { purpose: purpose } }
      response.parsed_body["challenge"]
    end

    def webauthn_challenge(purpose: nil)
      ActionPack::WebAuthn::PublicKeyCredential::Options.new(challenge_purpose: purpose).challenge
    end

    def webauthn_private_key
      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY
    end

    def build_attestation_params(challenge:)
      credential_id = SecureRandom.random_bytes(32)
      auth_data = build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id: credential_id)

      {
        passkey: {
          client_data_json: webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.create"),
          attestation_object: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(ATTESTATION_OBJECT_CBOR_PREFIX + auth_data, padding: false),
          transports: [ "internal" ]
        }
      }
    end

    def build_assertion_params(challenge:, credential:, sign_count: 1)
      client_data_json = webauthn_client_data_json(challenge: challenge, type: "webauthn.get")
      authenticator_data = build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count: sign_count)
      signature = webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)

      {
        passkey: {
          id: credential.credential_id,
          client_data_json: client_data_json,
          authenticator_data: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(authenticator_data, padding: false),
          signature: Base64.urlsafe_encode64(signature, padding: false)
        }
      }
    end

    def webauthn_client_data_json(challenge:, type:)
      { challenge: challenge, origin: "http://www.example.com", type: type }.to_json
    end

    # Attestation auth data includes the attested credential (public key + credential ID).
    def build_attestation_auth_data(credential_id:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),   # rp_id_hash
        [ 0x45 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV + AT
        [ 0 ].pack("N"),                            # sign_count
        "\x00" * 16,                                # aaguid
        [ credential_id.bytesize ].pack("n"),       # credential_id_length
        credential_id,
        COSE_PUBLIC_KEY
      ].join.b
    end

    # Assertion auth data is simpler — no attested credential.
    def build_assertion_auth_data(sign_count:)
      [
        Digest::SHA256.digest("www.example.com"),
        [ 0x05 ].pack("C"),                         # flags: UP + UV
        [ sign_count ].pack("N")
      ].join.b
    end

    def webauthn_sign(authenticator_data, client_data_json)
      signed_data = authenticator_data + Digest::SHA256.digest(client_data_json)
      WEBAUTHN_PRIVATE_KEY.sign("SHA256", signed_data)
    end
end

Okay, here's the deal: I'm staring at this drag-and-drop implementation, and something feels off. Why are we even considering `turbo-stream` for drag-and-drop when background persistence (`responseKind: "json"`) already exists and seems perfect for it? I've got to break down *every* requirement, and *every* edge case, and figure out the best approach.

First, I'm going to eliminate the obvious bad implementations: I *cannot* have the board snap back to the card's old position after a drop and then jump to the new column later. I also cannot have *anything* shifting after the drop, as that violates the immediate feel that's crucial for drag and drop.

This brings me to the fundamental decision: `turbo-stream` versus `json`? With `turbo-stream`, I have these cascading issues: the card visually shifts (color, stamps, timestamps, counts), the state of collapsed columns might become unstable, and potentially I could be stripping drag-and-drop attributes mid-drag! It feels overly complex and risky. Not only that, but existing `turbo-stream` code might break because we don't handle some of these endpoints in a *Turbo Stream* way.

Then I look at the `json` option. It's clean: use the existing `format.json` responses, get the background save, and broadcast refreshes for other tabs. This looks a lot easier. Is there an interaction that could be out of sync? It does not seem like it! Existing tests pass! 

The `json` option would allow a user to immediately drag the same card again to another column after a save. What about the hotkeys for actions like "postpone" or "close" or "assign to me"? The setup of "drag and drop" does not break anything!

So, background `json` persistence it is. It's a much more elegant solution: it is faster, has less risk, is easier to understand, and reuses existing code.

**Comprehensive System Test Plan for Drag-and-Drop Functionality**

Okay, time to get this test suite built out properly in `test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb`. I need to be absolutely thorough here, hitting every edge case and requirement for this drag-and-drop feature. Let's break it down methodically.

First, I need to test dragging a card from the "Maybe?" column into a custom column. This has to cover both collapsed and expanded states of the target column. I need to verify that card counts update instantly, that the `card.column` attribute is persisted correctly on the server, and the `--card-color` CSS variable updates to reflect the new column's color.

Next, I have to ensure dragging *between* custom columns works as intended. Specifically, if I drag from an "In progress" column to a "Triage" column, I must make sure it respects the column's sorting preference. If "Triage" has a custom order like `[logo (golden), layout]`, a non-golden card like "text" should land *after* "logo" and *before* "layout", resulting in `[logo, text, layout]`, and any golden card should land first.

Then I will need to test all transitions to "Done" and "Not Now" states. Dragging to "Done" (`#closed-cards`) should close the card (`card.closed? == true`) and place it at the top. Moving a card to "Not Now" (`#not-now`) should postpone it (`card.postponed? == true`), and it must take the top position even if there's an existing golden postponed card.

I will need to account for dragging *out* of those states too: Dragging a card out of "Done" back to "Maybe?", a custom column, or "Not Now" should reopen the card and re-set its column/status, remove any gray closed styling, and update the color. The same needs to be tested for dragging cards out of "Not Now."

I also want to make sure the expected behavior happens when dragging *within* the same column. If I drag "layout" onto "logo" in "Triage", I need to ensure that the target container doesn't get the `.drag-and-drop__hover-container` class, that the cards' order doesn't change, and that no unnecessary network requests are sent.

Of course, the visual styles must also be tested. The dragged card needs the `.drag-and-drop__dragged-item` class during the drag, which should dim it using `opacity: 0.6`. The target column must get `.drag-and-drop__hover-container` (the highlight effect) under the pointer, which should disappear on `dragleave`, moving to another column, `drop`, or `dragend`.

I need to nail down the "instant optimistic drop" behavior. I'm going to use `RequestInterceptor` (or a `window.fetch` wrapper) to pause the network save request. I'll drop the card *while* the request is paused. Immediately after the drop (before the server response!), I'll assert that the card is already in the target column in its correct sorted position, that it's gone from the source, that counts are updated, and that the visual classes are removed. I'll record the exact card ID and `getBoundingClientRect()` order *before* releasing the request, and then ensure that everything *stays put* after the save goes through and the card reloads in the database. I'll then reload the page and expand the column to confirm the server render is consistent. This is the crux of the user experience, and I need to make certain that there's no shifting or unexpected behavior.

Lastly, I need to test for scenarios with empty columns, and with Turbo morph/broadcast refreshes. An empty column should show a "Drag cards here" message. Dragging a card into it should immediately hide the message, and dragging the last card *out* of the expanded column should show it again. I need to verify that drag-and-drop still functions correctly after a Turbo morph or broadcast refresh.

With all of this verified, I can write this suite with confidence. Let's get to work!

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @board = boards(:writebook)
  end

  test "dragging a card across columns and statuses updates the board and persists" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    on_hold = columns(:writebook_on_hold)

    visit board_url(@board)

    # Maybe? -> In progress (collapsed column)
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(in_progress)}"))

    within("#maybe") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all }
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2" }
    wait_for { card.reload.column == in_progress }

    # Expand In progress and verify card is first and has column color
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(card, :article), dom_id(cards(:text), :article) ], card_ids_in_list
    end

    # In progress -> On Hold (another custom column)
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(on_hold)}"))
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all }
    within("##{dom_id(on_hold)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1" }
    wait_for { card.reload.column == on_hold }

    # Expand On Hold, then drag On Hold -> Not Now
    within("##{dom_id(on_hold)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(on_hold)} .blank-slate--drag"

    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#not-now"))
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(on_hold)} .blank-slate--drag", text: "Drag cards here"
    within("#not-now") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1" }
    wait_for { card.reload.postponed? }

    # Expand Not Now, then drag Not Now -> Done
    within("#not-now") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#closed-cards"))
    within("#not-now") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all }
    within("#closed-cards") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2" }
    wait_for { card.reload.closed? }

    # Expand Done, then drag Done -> Maybe?
    within("#closed-cards") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#maybe"))
    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    within("#closed-cards") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all }
    wait_for { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }
  end

  test "columns keep their own order: golden cards stay ahead of non-golden cards and dragging within a column does not reorder" do
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    logo = cards(:logo)       # golden, in Triage
    layout = cards(:layout)   # non-golden, in Triage
    buy_domain = cards(:buy_domain) # non-golden, in Maybe?

    visit board_url(@board)

    # Expand Triage; initial order is [logo (golden), layout]
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ], card_ids_in_list
    end

    # Try dragging layout above logo within Triage — order must not change
    find("##{dom_id(layout, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(logo, :article)}"))
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ], card_ids_in_list
      assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2", visible: :all
    end

    # Drag non-golden buy_domain from Maybe? onto Triage — lands after golden logo, before non-golden layout
    find("##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(triage)}"))
    expected_order = [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ]
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end

    wait_for { buy_domain.reload.column == triage }

    # Reload page and confirm server order matches optimistic order identically
    visit board_url(@board)
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end
  end

  test "dropping is instant before save completes and nothing shifts afterwards" do
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    logo = cards(:logo)
    layout = cards(:layout)
    buy_domain = cards(:buy_domain)

    visit board_url(@board)
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(triage)} ##{dom_id(logo, :article)}"

    # Hold the outgoing save request in flight so we can inspect DOM state before save completes
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__originalFetch = window.fetch
      window.__heldSaveResolve = null
      window.fetch = function(...args) {
        return new Promise(resolve => {
          window.__heldSaveResolve = () => resolve(window.__originalFetch.apply(this, args))
        })
      }
    JS

    find("##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(triage)}"))

    # Server has NOT saved yet
    assert_nil buy_domain.reload.column
    assert_no_selector ".drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
    assert_no_selector ".drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Yet the board is ALREADY in its final state
    expected_order = [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ]
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}"
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end

    rect_before_save = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}').getBoundingClientRect().toJSON()")

    # Release the save request and wait for persistence
    page.execute_script("window.__heldSaveResolve(); window.fetch = window.__originalFetch;")
    wait_for { buy_domain.reload.column == triage }

    # Nothing shifted afterwards
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end
    rect_after_save = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}').getBoundingClientRect().toJSON()")
    assert_equal rect_before_save["top"], rect_after_save["top"]
    assert_equal rect_before_save["left"], rect_after_save["left"]
  end

  test "dragged card dims and hovered target column lights up while source column does not" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)

    visit board_url(@board)

    card_id = dom_id(card, :article)
    triage_id = dom_id(triage)

    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const card = document.getElementById("#{card_id}")
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS

    assert_selector "##{card_id}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
    opacity = page.evaluate_script("getComputedStyle(document.getElementById('#{card_id}')).opacity")
    assert_equal "0.6", opacity

    # Hovering over the card's own column does NOT light it up
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const maybe = document.getElementById("maybe")
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#maybe.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Hovering over another column lights it up
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const triage = document.getElementById("#{triage_id}")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS
    assert_selector "##{triage_id}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Leaving the column removes the highlight, and dragend un-dims the card
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const triage = document.getElementById("#{triage_id}")
      const card = document.getElementById("#{card_id}")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragend", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "##{triage_id}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"
    assert_no_selector "##{card_id}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
  end

  test "cards remain draggable after a Turbo broadcast refresh" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    visit board_url(@board)
    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all

    cards(:layout).update!(title: "Updated elsewhere")
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    within("##{dom_id(columns(:writebook_triage))}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_selector "h3", text: "Updated elsewhere", wait: 5

    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(in_progress)}"))
    wait_for { card.reload.column == in_progress }
  end

  private
    def card_ids_in_list
      all(".cards__list .card", visible: :all).map { |el| el[:id] }
    end

    def wait_for(timeout: 5)
      deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + timeout
      until yield
        raise "Timed out waiting for condition" if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
        sleep 0.05
      end
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Eureka! Drag-and-Drop Click Prevention!**

Okay, this is fantastic! I was poring over that event log and it just *clicked*. Look at this sequence: `mousemove`, `mousedown`, `dragstart`, `dragover`, `dragover`, `dragend`, `mouseup`, `click`. What's happening is that when a drag ends without a drop in Chrome/WebDriver, Selenium generates a synthetic `mouseup` and then *immediately* a `click` event on the link – right after the `dragend` – and it's navigating away from the board! This also happens in real browsers too, given specific pointer or touchpad sequences or even via WebDriver!

The solution, though? It's elegant. To prevent this phantom click after a drag, I need a few simple steps. In `dragStart`, I'll set `this.#suppressNextClick = true`, or disable pointer events on `.card__link` while dragging. Another option is intercepting the click in the capture phase for one tick after `dragend`:

// In connect():
this.preventPostDragClick = this.#preventPostDragClick.bind(this)
this.element.addEventListener("click", this.preventPostDragClick, true)

And in `dragStart`:
`this.justDragged = true`

And the `#preventPostDragClick` method:

#preventPostDragClick(event) {
  if (this.justDragged) {
    event.preventDefault()
    event.stopImmediatePropagation()
    this.justDragged = false
  }

This way, if a click *should* occur without a drag, `this.justDragged` is `false`, and the click functions normally. However, if a drag *did* start (`dragstart` set `this.justDragged = true`) and a trailing `mouseup` + `click` fires immediately after `dragend`, `#preventPostDragClick` intercepts it in the capture phase, preventing the unintended navigation! `setTimeout(..., 0)` clears `this.justDragged = false` on the next macrotask, allowing subsequent intentional clicks to work right away.

I'm incredibly grateful we wrote that Selenium test! It was the *only* way we would have discovered this quirk with Chrome and WebDriver firing that extra click after a canceled drag.

Alright, time to add this `#preventPostDragClick` to `app/javascript/controllers/drag_and_drop_controller.js`, clean up those debug statements in `test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb`, and add a test confirming that regular clicks still navigate to the card show page.

Here's my analysis of the issue, explained as if it's my own thought process:

**Eureka! I've Got It! The `setTimeout(..., 0)` Problem!**

Okay, so I've been digging into why that `this.justDragged` flag was being cleared prematurely in Selenium, and I think I've cracked it. Remember that event order we logged? It was something like "dragend:article_card_...", "mouseup:card__link", "click:card__link". The key is understanding how Selenium WebDriver's ActionBuilder interacts with the browser.

Essentially, `move_to(target)` doesn't directly trigger Chrome's `dragend`. Instead, the `pointer_up` event does, and that happens in a *different* browser IPC frame. The problem is that `setTimeout(..., 0)` is running *before* WebDriver finishes dispatching the `mouseup` and `click` events a few milliseconds later! I was worried that Turbo's `LinkClickObserver` (which listens on `window`/`document`) was catching the `click` *after* the `dragend`... which makes sense, since it can come 10-50ms later!

So, the solution? Forget the `0ms` timeout! I need to delay the clearing of `this.justDragged`. If I use `requestAnimationFrame` or, better yet, a `100ms` delay instead, that should do the trick. No human interaction is fast enough to perform a complete drag and *then* immediately start a new `mousedown + mouseup` click within 50ms. Setting `this.justDragged = false` on `mousedown` OR after `100ms` means that *any* real click starts with a fresh `mousedown`, which resets `this.justDragged = false` immediately, while any trailing `click` from the drag's `mouseup` has NO new `mousedown` before it and is 100% blocked!!

**Hold on, let's step back and consider the logic.** This `mousedown + 100ms` approach is *clean*. Think about this:

1.  **During the drag:** `dragstart` *correctly* sets `this.justDragged = true`.
2.  **When the drag *ends*** (`drop` or `dragend`): There is *no* `mousedown` between the `dragend` and a phantom `mouseup` + `click` sequence.
3.  **For *any* real click afterwards:** Even if it's just 1ms later, a real click *always* starts with a `mousedown` (or `pointerdown`) event BEFORE the `mouseup` + `click` events!
4.  **Therefore:**
    *   `pointerdown` / `mousedown` *immediately* sets `this.justDragged = false`.
    *   The `100ms` timeout ALSO clears `this.justDragged = false`, just in case a synthetic test dispatches a `.click()` directly in JavaScript without a preceding `mousedown` (which it *shouldn't* do, but just in case), but even 100ms is *long* enough to cover this scenario, in which case the phantom `click` would still be blocked.
    *   Meanwhile, any ghost `click` emitted from the drag's own `mouseup` (even 20ms after `dragend` in Selenium!) *sees* that `this.justDragged` is still `true` and gets suppressed!

I need to test this right now! Let's see if this fixes the Selenium issue!

Okay, that was a good start! Now, I need to really dig into `test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb` and flush out the edge cases. Let's make sure we've covered everything.

First, I'm thinking about how golden cards interact with existing columns. Specifically:

What happens when I drag a gilded card (like `buy_domain`, which has been gilded with `buy_domain.gild`) *into* a column (`Triage`) that already has a mix of golden (`logo`) and non-golden cards (`layout`)? Since the newly triaged `buy_domain` is golden *and* recent, it should land at the top (`[buy_domain, logo, layout]`), and this should be the case immediately and persist after a reload!

2.  Next, let's look at non-golden cards dragged into "Done" or "Not Now." We already know these columns, which are `.postponed.latest` and `.closed.recently_closed_first`, *don't* sort golden cards first. What if a golden card (`logo`) is already in one of these columns, and then a non-golden card (`buy_domain`) is dragged in? It should be `[buy_domain, logo]` immediately and after a reload, because the golden card sort is not applicable.

3.  The *visual* effects need to be flawless on drop. I want to test that things like card color, closed stamps, bubbles, and assignees update **immediately** – before even a save is confirmed – and that there's no shifting afterward. So, if a closed card (`shipping`) in "Done" with a closed stamp, a gray color, and hidden assignees, is dragged into "In Progress," I should immediately see the color change, the stamp disappear, the assignees become visible, etc. The reverse should happen when dragging an open card with a stalled bubble into "Done" – it should immediately remove the bubble and hide the assignees.

4.  I also want to fully test the onboarding flow. If a user creates a brand-new column (using the "+" button) and then immediately drags a card into that new column without a page reload, it should work seamlessly.

5.  Finally, let's cover some crucial edge cases based on UI/permissions:
    *   On a small viewport (less than 640px), cards should *not* be draggable, and empty columns should show the "No cards here" message.
    *   On public boards, the cards should *not* be draggable.

require "application_system_test_case"

class DragAndDropTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  include ActionView::RecordIdentifier

  setup do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))
    @board = boards(:writebook)
  end

  test "dragging a card across columns and statuses updates the board and persists" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)
    on_hold = columns(:writebook_on_hold)

    visit board_url(@board)

    # Maybe? -> In progress (collapsed column)
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(in_progress)}"))

    within("#maybe") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all }
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2" }
    wait_for { card.reload.column == in_progress }

    # Expand In progress and verify card is first and has column color
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(card, :article), dom_id(cards(:text), :article) ], card_ids_in_list
    end

    # In progress -> On Hold (another custom column)
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(on_hold)}"))
    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all }
    within("##{dom_id(on_hold)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1" }
    wait_for { card.reload.column == on_hold }

    # Expand On Hold, then drag On Hold -> Not Now
    within("##{dom_id(on_hold)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(on_hold)} .blank-slate--drag"

    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#not-now"))
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(on_hold)} .blank-slate--drag", text: "Drag cards here"
    within("#not-now") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1" }
    wait_for { card.reload.postponed? }

    # Expand Not Now, then drag Not Now -> Done
    within("#not-now") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#closed-cards"))
    within("#not-now") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "0", visible: :all }
    within("#closed-cards") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2" }
    wait_for { card.reload.closed? }

    # Expand Done, then drag Done -> Maybe?
    within("#closed-cards") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("#maybe"))
    assert_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(card, :article)}"
    within("#closed-cards") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1", visible: :all }
    wait_for { card.reload.awaiting_triage? }

    # Clicking a card normally still navigates to the card page
    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)} .card__link").click
    assert_current_path card_path(card)
  end

  test "columns keep their own order: golden cards stay ahead of non-golden cards and dragging within a column does not reorder" do
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    logo = cards(:logo)             # golden, in Triage
    layout = cards(:layout)         # non-golden, in Triage
    buy_domain = cards(:buy_domain) # non-golden, in Maybe?
    text = cards(:text)             # in In progress; gild it to test golden card insertion
    Current.set(user: users(:kevin)) { text.gild }

    visit board_url(@board)

    # Expand Triage; initial order is [logo (golden), layout]
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ], card_ids_in_list
    end

    # Try dragging layout onto logo within Triage — order must not change and page must stay on board
    find("##{dom_id(layout, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(logo, :article)}"))
    assert_current_path board_path(@board)
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ], card_ids_in_list
      assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "2", visible: :all
    end

    # Drag non-golden buy_domain from Maybe? onto Triage — lands after golden logo, before non-golden layout
    find("##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(triage)}"))
    expected_order = [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ]
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end
    wait_for { buy_domain.reload.column == triage }

    # Drag golden text from In progress onto Triage — lands ahead of older golden logo
    within("##{dom_id(columns(:writebook_in_progress))}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    find("##{dom_id(text, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(triage)}"))
    expected_order_with_golden = [ dom_id(text, :article), dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ]
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order_with_golden, card_ids_in_list
    end
    wait_for { text.reload.column == triage }

    # Reload page and confirm server order matches optimistic order identically
    visit board_url(@board)
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order_with_golden, card_ids_in_list
    end
  end

  test "Done and Not Now order purely by recency even when existing card is golden" do
    logo = cards(:logo)             # golden
    buy_domain = cards(:buy_domain) # non-golden

    Current.set(user: users(:kevin)) { logo.postpone }

    visit board_url(@board)

    find("##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}").drag_to(find("#not-now"))
    wait_for { buy_domain.reload.postponed? }

    expected_order = [ dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(logo, :article) ]
    within("#not-now") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end

    visit board_url(@board)
    within("#not-now") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end
  end

  test "dropping is instant before save completes and nothing shifts afterwards" do
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)
    logo = cards(:logo)
    layout = cards(:layout)
    buy_domain = cards(:buy_domain)

    visit board_url(@board)
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_selector "##{dom_id(triage)} ##{dom_id(logo, :article)}"

    # Hold the outgoing save request in flight so we can inspect DOM state before save completes
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      window.__originalFetch = window.fetch
      window.__heldSaveResolve = null
      window.fetch = function(...args) {
        return new Promise(resolve => {
          window.__heldSaveResolve = () => resolve(window.__originalFetch.apply(this, args))
        })
      }
    JS

    find("##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(triage)}"))

    # Server has NOT saved yet
    assert_nil buy_domain.reload.column
    assert_no_selector ".drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
    assert_no_selector ".drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Yet the board is ALREADY in its final state (position, count, and column card color)
    expected_order = [ dom_id(logo, :article), dom_id(buy_domain, :article), dom_id(layout, :article) ]
    assert_no_selector "#maybe ##{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}"
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
      assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "3", visible: :all
    end
    card_color = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}').style.getPropertyValue('--card-color')")
    assert_equal triage.color.to_s, card_color

    rect_before_save = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}').getBoundingClientRect().toJSON()")

    # Release the save request and wait for persistence
    page.execute_script("window.__heldSaveResolve(); window.fetch = window.__originalFetch;")
    wait_for { buy_domain.reload.column == triage }

    # Nothing shifted afterwards
    within("##{dom_id(triage)}") do
      assert_equal expected_order, card_ids_in_list
    end
    rect_after_save = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(buy_domain, :article)}').getBoundingClientRect().toJSON()")
    assert_equal rect_before_save["top"], rect_after_save["top"]
    assert_equal rect_before_save["left"], rect_after_save["left"]
  end

  test "dragging a closed card into an active column immediately updates its color and removes closed stamp" do
    shipping = cards(:shipping) # closed
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    visit board_url(@board)
    within("#closed-cards") { find(".cards__expander").click }

    find("##{dom_id(shipping, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(in_progress)}"))
    wait_for { shipping.reload.open? && shipping.column == in_progress }

    within("##{dom_id(in_progress)}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_no_selector "##{dom_id(shipping, :article)} .card__closed", visible: :all
    card_color = page.evaluate_script("document.getElementById('#{dom_id(shipping, :article)}').style.getPropertyValue('--card-color')")
    assert_equal in_progress.color.to_s, card_color
  end

  test "dragging a card into a newly created column works immediately" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)

    visit board_url(@board)

    click_on "New column"
    fill_in "column[name]", with: "QA"
    send_keys :enter

    assert_selector ".cards__expander-title", text: /QA/i
    new_column = @board.columns.find_by!(name: "QA")

    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(new_column)}"))
    within("##{dom_id(new_column)}") { assert_selector ".cards__expander-count", text: "1" }
    wait_for { card.reload.column == new_column }
  end

  test "dragged card dims and hovered target column lights up while source column does not" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    triage = columns(:writebook_triage)

    visit board_url(@board)

    card_id = dom_id(card, :article)
    triage_id = dom_id(triage)

    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const card = document.getElementById("#{card_id}")
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragstart", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS

    assert_selector "##{card_id}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
    opacity = page.evaluate_script("getComputedStyle(document.getElementById('#{card_id}')).opacity")
    assert_equal "0.6", opacity

    # Hovering over the card's own column does NOT light it up
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const maybe = document.getElementById("maybe")
      maybe.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "#maybe.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Hovering over another column lights it up
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const triage = document.getElementById("#{triage_id}")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragover", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true, dataTransfer: new DataTransfer() }))
    JS
    assert_selector "##{triage_id}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"

    # Leaving the column removes the highlight, and dragend un-dims the card
    page.execute_script(<<~JS)
      const triage = document.getElementById("#{triage_id}")
      const card = document.getElementById("#{card_id}")
      triage.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragleave", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
      card.dispatchEvent(new DragEvent("dragend", { bubbles: true, cancelable: true }))
    JS
    assert_no_selector "##{triage_id}.drag-and-drop__hover-container"
    assert_no_selector "##{card_id}.drag-and-drop__dragged-item"
  end

  test "cards remain draggable after a Turbo broadcast refresh" do
    card = cards(:buy_domain)
    in_progress = columns(:writebook_in_progress)

    visit board_url(@board)
    assert_selector "turbo-cable-stream-source[connected]", visible: :all

    Current.set(user: users(:kevin)) { cards(:layout).update!(title: "Updated elsewhere") }
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: Turbo::Streams::BroadcastStreamJob

    within("##{dom_id(columns(:writebook_triage))}") { find(".cards__expander").click }
    assert_selector "h3", text: "Updated elsewhere", wait: 5

    find("##{dom_id(card, :article)}").drag_to(find("##{dom_id(in_progress)}"))
    wait_for { card.reload.column == in_progress }
  end

  private
    def card_ids_in_list
      all(".cards__list .card", visible: :all).map { |el| el[:id] }
    end

    def wait_for(timeout: 5)
      deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + timeout
      until yield
        raise "Timed out waiting for condition" if Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
        sleep 0.05
      end
    end
end

messages.content:
I have implemented board drag-and-drop so people can change a card's column or status instantly by dragging it across the board:

- **Stimulus controller (`app/javascript/controllers/drag_and_drop_controller.js`)**:
  - Enables HTML5 drag-and-drop on desktop board viewports (`>= 640px`) and preserves `draggable` attributes across Turbo morphs and frame renders.
  - Applies `.drag-and-drop__dragged-item` to dim the dragged card and `.drag-and-drop__hover-container` to highlight valid target columns while ignoring the card's current column so cards move between places rather than reordering within one.
  - Updates the DOM optimistically on `drop` before the save completes: places the card in the target column's canonical sort position (golden cards first for `Maybe?` and custom columns, newest first for `Not Now` and `Done`), updates card color/status classes/stamps/timestamps/counts immediately, and persists via serialized background JSON requests (`keepalive: true`) so nothing shifts afterwards.
- **Board, column, and card views/helpers**:
  - Wired `drag-and-drop` on `.card-columns`, configured drop URLs/methods/metadata on `column_tag` (`Not Now`, `Maybe?`, custom columns, and `Done`), marked card previews as `item` targets, and rendered column blank-slate placeholders unconditionally inside `.cards__list` so `"Drag cards here"` toggles immediately via CSS `:has(.card)`.
- **Tests (`test/system/drag_and_drop_test.rb`)**:
  - Added end-to-end system tests covering all column/status transitions, column ordering rules, drag/hover styles, instant optimistic drop with zero shifting after save, newly created columns, and post-broadcast-refresh draggability.

Submitting the final output now.
